Interview Questions: How do you use the Myntra Wishlist?
Responder 1:
I save products that I like but don't want to purchase immediately. I use the wishlist as a shortlist while I compare products and make up my mind.

For me, adding something to the wishlist doesn't necessarily mean I'm going to buy it. If I like something but I'm not 100% convinced, I'll save it. Then I'll come back later, check the reviews, compare it with other products and decide whether it's actually worth buying.
Responder 2:
I use the wishlist a lot. If I like something but I'm not sure whether it'll actually look good on me, I'll save it. I don't want to make the decision immediately.

Sometimes I save five or six similar products. Later I'll remove most of them and keep maybe one or two.
Responder 3: I save products that catch my attention so I can come back to them when I actually need something.
Responder 4: I use it almost like a watchlist. If I really like something, I'll save it and see whether I still want it after a few days
Responder 5: I save products mainly for reference or to look at later.

Basically, adding it to the wishlist gives me time to make a decision without losing the product.

I wanted to see customer photos and maybe find someone on Instagram or YouTube wearing something similar.

Interview Questions: When you find an item you really like but hesitate to buy, how much does it bother you?
Responder 1:
The quality one is definitely the biggest. With fashion, you can't actually touch the product before buying it. A picture can make something look premium, but you don't know how the fabric will actually feel.

Size is the second biggest issue for me. Even if I know my usual size, different brands and different fits can be inconsistent. If I have to return something, it's not impossible, but it becomes an extra task.

Delivery isn't a huge issue for me because most of the time I'm not buying something for a specific date. If I need something urgently, then obviously it matters more.

Refund is somewhere in the middle. I don't usually worry about it before purchasing, but if I've already had a bad return experience, then I become more cautious.
Responder 2:
Quality matters, but for me it's more about whether the product looks the way I expect it to.

I don't really worry much about delivery. Most of the time I'm not buying something urgently.
Responder 3:
Honestly, I don't worry too much about refunds. I've ordered online enough that I know how returns generally work.

Quality also isn't my biggest concern. Of course I want the product to be good, but if I really need something, I'll read reviews and make the decision.

Delivery is different. If I'm buying something for a wedding or an office event, getting it late makes the purchase useless. So delivery becomes a much bigger issue when there's a deadline.
Responder 4: My biggest hesitation is whether I feel I'm getting enough value for the money.
Responder 5: These aren't really my concerns because I don't buy much online in the first place.

My main issue isn't a bad Myntra experience. I just find that similar products are often available in local markets for less.

I've done this several times. I'll see a bag online, show the picture to a shopkeeper and ask if he has something similar.

Interview Questions: How do you currently overcome uncertainty regarding whether an item will fit properly?
Responder 1:
I first check the size chart, but I don't completely depend on it. I look at reviews and try to find people who have mentioned their height, weight or usual size.

If someone says something like ‘I'm 5'10, around 75 kg and bought a Large,’ that's much more useful to me than just seeing a generic size chart.

I also compare the measurements with clothes I already own that fit me well. If it's a brand I've purchased before, I'm much more confident because I already know how their sizing works.

For a new brand, I'm much more cautious.
Responder 2:
I check the size chart, but that's not enough for me.

I look at the model's measurements if they're available, then compare that with myself. Customer reviews are also useful, especially when someone says what size they bought and how it fit.

If I can't find enough information, I'll usually save the product and wait rather than buy it immediately.”
Responder 3:
I'm fairly comfortable with sizing because I mostly buy brands I've bought before.

If it's a new brand, I'll check the size chart and reviews. But I'm not going to spend 30 minutes analysing measurements for a normal ₹1,000–₹2,000 item.

If I feel the sizing looks risky, I'll simply choose another product.
Responder 4: I check the size chart and reviews. If I've bought from the brand before, I already know my size.
Responder 5: For bags, fitting isn't really an issue. I physically check the size and compartments in the shop.

Interview Questions: What specific information, guarantee, or feature (excluding discounts or credits) is currently MISSING from the Myntra wishlist that would make you purchase more frequently?
Responder 1:
I think the wishlist needs more information that helps me make the final decision. Right now it's basically a place where I save the product.

I'd want to see genuine customer photos, more useful fit information and some indication of whether the product actually matches what customers expected.

For example, if most people who bought a shirt say the fabric is thinner than expected, I'd want to know that before buying. Similarly, if people with a similar body type are consistently buying Medium and saying it fits well, that would give me confidence.

Basically, I want the wishlist to help me decide, not just remind me that I saved something.
Responder 2:
Real-life representation of the product.
I'd like the wishlist to show customer photos and videos automatically instead of making me search for them elsewhere.
Even better would be showing the product on different body types. If I could see the same shirt on someone skinny, someone broad-shouldered and someone around my body type, I'd have a much better idea of whether it would suit me.

The product page tells me what the clothes are. It doesn't always tell me what they'll look like on an actual person
Responder 3:
I'd actually like the wishlist to help me decide whether I still need something.

For example, if I saved a dress three weeks ago, maybe Myntra could remind me that I saved it and show me similar things I've already bought. Or it could show styling ideas or occasions where the product might work.
Responder 4: I'd like better comparison information—similar products, what makes this product different, and whether people think it's actually worth the price. That would help me make a decision faster.
Responder 5:
Maybe actual material details and dimensions would help. For a laptop bag, I want to know whether my laptop will fit, how many compartments it has and how strong the material is.

But even then, I'd still compare it with what's available locally.
